MAPF-POST is a novel postprocessor that takes a MAPF solution and creates a kinematically feasible schedule for differential-drive robots, which is guaranteed to avoid collisions, and which can be executed on real robots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce MAPF- POST, a postprocessing algorithm that converts a MAPF solution into a plan-execution sequence.
we provide the first MAPF solver for non-holonomic differential-drive robots that can handle hundreds of robots and provides a guaranteed safety margin.
we introduce a new MAPF problem, MAPF with kinematic constraints, and propose a novel algorithm, MAPF-POST, to solve the problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can leverage the power of MAPF to solve challenging multi-agent path finding problems, even when the agents are subject to kinodynamic constraints.
MAPF solvers can be used in practice to solve large instances of the problem, and postprocessing is a practical way of handling kinematic constraints in a MAPF setting.
